pr_title: usb: device_next: fix CDC NCM datagram pointers processing
pr_body:
The implementation should not assume that NDP is placed immediately
after NTH. According to the specification (revision 1.0), NDP can be
anywhere in the transfer buffer. There is also always a "terminating
zero datagram pointer entry", which we should also use to terminate the
datagram processing loop.

Fixes: #81960

issue_context.title: net: perf: Running on MacOS and NRF52840-DK
issue_context.body:
Note: long discussion in [Discord Subsystems USB](https://discord.com/channels/720317445772017664/1305952695995334657),  prior to filing a bug

**Describe the bug**

My ultimate goal is to use USB-CDC NCM as a networking adapter to communicate with iPadOS via UDP sockets.  I am struggling to get this stack working, so my first step is to get the net/zperf sample to compile and be recognized by MacOS as a network device.

The current state is that I am using a nRF52840-DK as a reference board and while I can compile and run zperf, I have found a few issues that in the sample with stack overflow and once these are fixed, MacOS recognizes the NCM device but does not show it as Active so it cannot be connected to.  Instead, I see:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fd1147bc-adba-463f-91fc-411a3d44a891)

and attempts to get the device manually connected (Limit IP address tracking -> Off, TCP/IP Configure IPv4 -> Manually, IP Address 192.0.2.2) have not worked.

See also:

Discussion on CDC-ECM working with MacOS (NetworkConnection Management needed)
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/69209

Platforms such as macOS, iOS and iPadOS will not perform DHCP negotiation with autoconf fallback without the interface being "connected".
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/discussions/69211 @donusry-privoro

 - What target platform are you using?

MacOS Sequoia 15.1.1, Apple M1
nRF52840-DK

 - What have you tried to diagnose or workaround this issue?

Switch to USB-Next Device Stack
Simplify approach to use off the shelf sample rather than writing code from scratch
Increase log level
Long discussions on Discord with @josuah 
Review all previous discussions I could find of USB ECM/NCM and MacOS/iPadOS
Increase Stack Sizes to mitigate stack overflows in off the shelf sample code
Run under Ozone debugger
Install Arch Linux and use it to get a 'Linux eye view' of networking and usb device diagnostics
Patch usbd_cdc_ncm.c to set errno = ENOTSUP; in usbd_cdc_ncm_ctd(...) per discussion with @josuah 

 - Is this a regression?

No, AFAIK until recently MacOS/iPadOS interoperability was not possible due to ECM limitations in the USB Previous stack.

**To Reproduce**

```
west build -p -b nrf52840dk/nrf52840 samples/net/zperf -DEXTRA_CONF_FILE="overlay-usbd_next.conf" -DDTC_OVERLAY_FILE="usbd_next_ncm.overlay"
west flash
```

Modifications to prj.conf to deal with memfault stack overflows detected when running under Ozone debugger with RTT debug logging enabled.  Found stack overflows on both netmgmt and usbd threads.

```
CONFIG_MAIN_STACK_SIZE=4096
CONFIG_NET_MGMT_EVENT_STACK_SIZE=4096
CONFIG_USBD_THREAD_STACK_SIZE=4096
```

Modifications to pro.conf to add DBG_LOG levels and switch to using RTT logging:

```
CONFIG_DEBUG=y
CONFIG_DEBUG_INFO=y
CONFIG_DEBUG_OPTIMIZATIONS=y

CONFIG_PRINTK=y
CONFIG_LOG_MODE_IMMEDIATE=y
CONFIG_LOG_BACKEND_SHOW_COLOR=n
CONFIG_LOG_PRINTK=y

CONFIG_USE_SEGGER_RTT=y
CONFIG_LOG_BACKEND_RTT=y
CONFIG_LOG_BACKEND_RTT_MODE_DROP=y

CONFIG_USBD_LOG_LEVEL_DBG=y
CONFIG_UDC_DRIVER_LOG_LEVEL_DBG=y
CONFIG_USBD_CDC_NCM_LOG_LEVEL_DBG=y

CONFIG_NET_STATISTICS=y
CONFIG_NET_IF_LOG_LEVEL_DBG=y
CONFIG_NET_L2_ETHERNET_LOG_LEVEL_DBG=y
CONFIG_NET_SOCKETS_LOG_LEVEL_DBG=y
CONFIG_NET_CONN_LOG_LEVEL_DBG=y
CONFIG_NET_CONTEXT_LOG_LEVEL_DBG=y
CONFIG_NET_TCP_LOG_LEVEL_DBG=y
```

**Expected behavior**

An 'out of the box' example of USB CDC ECM/NCM that interoperates with MacOS, either samples/net/zperf or samples/net/sockets/echo_server, preferably including autoconf or dhcp so that it 'just works'.

**Impact**

Weeks into trying to get Zephyr USB CDC ECM or NCM to work with no joy :-)

The Windows 10 (UsbNcm) driver is not working flawlessly with our implementation, and I am reluctant to have a workaround on our end. The issue is now it handles segment delineation, I observed that the Windows 10 driver does not use ZLP or padding to create a short packet for the case the transfer is multiple of MPS but smaller than the dwNtbOutMaxSize. (Linux kernel driver uses padding for "Generic CDC-NCM devices", macOS driver (Ventura) and our implementation uses ZLP). I have not had time to test Windows 11 yet.

Sounds like this issue with ZLP may have been corrected in Windows 11:

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/1531925/difference-in-usb-ncm-class-driver-behavior-for-wi

> As per this Ethernet Control Model specification, the host driver of an NCM device’s communication interface is expected to send a Zero-Length Packet (ZLP) when the Nth packet equals the maximum packet size. This specification is correctly adhered to by the host driver in Windows 11, which sends the ZLP as expected. However, this is not the case in Windows 10. We have confirmed this discrepancy through Lacro and Wireshark logs. Consequently, our compact USB NCM device does not operate correctly with the UsbNcm.sys driver in Windows 10.

I'm happy to run a test on Windows 11 and see if the issue is corrected, what are your repo steps and observed failure?
